item.title: Pump Up The Jam – Geocache of the Week
item.description:
Traditional
GCA9ERG
by Nana_Bee
Difficulty:
1.5
Terrain:
1.5
Location:
Massachusetts, United States
N 41° 40.731′ W 071° 00.069′

This Geocache of the Week is an ode to an American culinary classic, the peanut butter and jelly sandwich. Unassuming on the outside, sweet and savory on the inside, the PB&J is a nostalgic lunchbox staple.

Pump Up The Jam (GCA9ERG) lives up to the humble legacy of its namesake. At first glance, this appears to be an ordinary cache hidden inside a birdhouse. But geocachers familiar with Nana_Bee’s caches know there’s more to this cache than meets the eye.

As a multi-media artist, I love to build caches that allow me to flex my creative muscles. I like to make caches that are unique and unusual… Pump Up The Jam is a very simple gadget cache that anyone can solve in less than a minute, but it’s sure to put a smile on your face… or make you hungry.” —Nana_Bee

It’s the attention to detail that really sets this design apart; the inside of the cache is decorated with grape-purple accents (although raspberry-red would also be acceptable), and a magnetic blob of jelly holds a table knife, the perfect TOTT to spread some inspiration to struggling geocachers.

No PB&J is complete without peanut butter! The missing ingredient and the logbook are sandwiched behind a secret panel disguised as a slice of bread, while a hovering bee guards the com‘bee’nation lock.

If this cache leaves your mouth watering for your own cache creation, take a page out of Nana_Bee’s recipe book and get creative!

It doesn’t have to cost an arm a leg to build something fun and unique. Check your scrap wood pile, your junk drawer, and yard sales for interesting objects to work with. Don’t worry if it’s not a work of art, as long as it works.” —Nana_Bee

item.title: Celebrate 25 Years of Geocaching with The GeoGuessr Challenge
item.description:
We’re excited to announce a limited-time collaboration between Geocaching HQ and GeoGuessr in celebration of a major milestone—25 years of geocaching!

GeoGuessr is an interactive geography game that drops players into random locations around the world using Google Street View. Just like geocaching, players use navigation and deduction skills—aka geo-senses—to pinpoint the location. The closer the guess, the more points they earn. This year, geocachers can once again earn a limited-time souvenir!

From iconic scenic vistas to remote hiking trails, The GeoGuessr Challenge features 25 locations from around the world, many inspired by the early days of geocaching.

As you play, you might notice some familiar places. Please note: The GeoGuessr Challenge doesn’t involve real-life geocaching. Instead, our goal is to showcase memorable locations, invite new explorers to our global community, and—most importantly—inspire future outdoor adventure!

To participate and earn a limited-time souvenir, complete the following steps:

  1. Create a free GeoGuessr account.
  2. Play the GeoGuessr Challenge between April 29-May 9 and find the tracking code.
  3. Discover the code at Geocaching.com before May 9, 2025 to earn a special souvenir.

NOTE: Geocaching HQ gives permission for this trackable to be discovered virtually.

For the best experience, we recommend playing on a computer or larger screen.

📍 Start The GeoGuessr Challenge

item.title: Blue Switch Day Hider Souvenir
item.description:
Time to hide your Blue Switch Day geocache!

It’s incredible to think that one small action could chart a course toward something so big. On May 2, 2000, that’s exactly what happened as the pivotal decision was made to flip the “Blue Switch,” leading to geocaching as we know it today.

This first hide started a chain of events that no one could have predicted. This eventually resulted in the game of geocaching, a global hobby with over 3.3 million geocaches! Now’s your chance to commemorate 25 years of geocaching by hiding a geocache and earning your Blue Switch Day hider souvenir

Blue Switch Day 2025 hider:

  • To earn this souvenir, submit a geocache for publication between May 1 and 31, 2025
  • Events and Adventure Labs not included
  • Submit your geocache for review by May 24, 2025

Learn more about the cache review process in our Help Center

item.title: Geocache Picker 101 — Geocache of the Week
item.description:
Traditional
GC8R2RA
by Trycacheus
Difficulty:
3.5
Terrain:
1.5
Location:
North Dakota, United States
N 48° 08.503 W 097° 30.923

Are you ready to unlock a whole new level of fun? We hope you don’t have a favorite geocache in mind because it’s time to pick your favorite one! This cache comes with some cool Tools of the Trade (TOTT) that will be your key to success.

Unlike the geocache description suggests, we aren’t picking the nose of our friends, but rather picking the nose of this Geocache of the Week, Geocache Picker 101 (GC8R2RA).

Gilby, North Dakota made a name for itself as the “amusement park of geocaching.” Many cachers plan trips to Gilby with the sole purpose of finding as many fun and unique caches as possible.

One of these amusing geocaches, GC8R2RA, is a creative gadget cache by Trycacheus, that puts anyone’s nose-picking… we mean lock-picking skills, to the test. The posted coordinates reveal an amusing sight to see.

A closer look reveals that the wooden knob is not just any, but one in the shape of a nose. Nearby are the necessary TOTT – picking devices, adding to the intrigue of this cache.

Suddenly the cache description makes a lot more sense. A nose… A pick… you got it, you have to pick the lock of this nose to get to the goods.

If you are not familiar with how lock picking works, check out this easy-to-understand explanation. Thankfully, the cache owner also provides instructions within the geocache itself, along with imagery to fully understand what needs to be done.

So you’re a lock-picking pro by now — but not so fast! Once you crack this wooden casing open, you find the next surprise… level 2!

Inside the wooden box is a bright green ammo can with an additional lock to be picked. As if the log sheet would reveal itself after just one lock!

Hopefully, you’re not in a hurry, as this cache proves to be thoughtfully time-consuming. To crack this cache, use the provided TOTT once more.

Getting inside is no easy feat. Many cachers logged entries stating that if it weren’t for someone else in their party, they would not have successfully solved this cache, and others report learning about their unknown lock-picking skills.

Patience and a good picking device are the clear winners here. If you can bring optimism and tenacity, you are sure to get to the magical log sheet along with definite bragging rights.

Nosey cachers will ‘snot’ give up until they crack this cache. Once the glorious final click is heard, the mechanism releases, granting access into the lime green ammo container.

A hard-earned log entry, no wonder picking noses has become a popular activity in Gilby. GC8R2RA has amassed over 600 logs and 263 Favorite points, as of 2025. A number sure to grow as more cachers make their way to this famed geocaching city.

A clever hide, Trycacheus is no stranger to fun gadget caches, writing in their profile:

“Hello, I’m Trycacheus and I live in Gilby, North Dakota. I enjoy spending time in the shop making unique caches. There aren’t many things to see in my hometown of Gilby so I like to place fun gadget caches for people to find.”
This cache is sure to give finders a chuckle while putting concentration and dexterity to the test.”

If you’ve ever wondered what it might be like to pick someone else’s nose, here is your chance!

What kind of gadget cache would you create?

item.title: New Treasures coming soon!
item.description:
Get ready—May is shaping up to be a memorable month for geocachers! We’re excited to celebrate Blue Switch Day, the 25th anniversary of geocaching, and the arrival of two new Treasure collections.

Two new collections, Classic trackables and Mystery books, will be available starting May 6 at 12:00 PM UTC. To start collecting Treasure from the Classic trackables collection, geocachers must first complete the Celebrating 25 years collection. To start collecting Treasure from the Mystery books collection, geocachers must first complete the Navigational tools collection.

Once you’ve completed the necessary prerequisite collections, you can collect Treasures by finding and logging geocaches that meet the criteria for either collection.

Starting May 6 at 12:00 PM UTC, you can view the criteria for the new collections by clicking the information symbol on the collection display on the Treasures page.These collections are not time-limited. You can collect the Treasure at your own pace.

Whether you’re still working on Geocaching origins or ready to start a new collection, here are a few things to keep in mind as you collect Treasure:

  • Sometimes, a single geocache meets the criteria for more than one Treasure. For example, the Traditional Cache egg and the Navigational tools Treasures have overlapping criteria. If a geocacher hasn’t collected the Traditional Cache egg and has not completed the Navigational tools collection, and they log a qualifying geocache, they will collect only one Treasure, randomly chosen from either collection.
  • If a log is deleted, the Treasure collected from that log is removed. To collect the Treasure again, find and log a different geocache that meets the criteria.

We value your feedback about the new Treasures feature and want to hear from you! Please share comments below or through the feedback form linked on the Treasures page.

item.title: A party, a platypus, and geofriends down under – The Sunbury Event Block Party (GCAP417) in Australia
item.description:
On a sunny weekend in March, geocachers gathered in the town of Sunbury for a party. Muggle the Puggle, a baby platypus, was the event’s adorable mascot who welcomed everyone to the festivities. The platypus, a unique animal only found in Australia, was a perfect addition to The Sunbury Event Block Party (GCAP417) that celebrated all the incredible things about geocaching in Australia over the last 25 years. It was an amazing experience full of friendly geocachers, passionate cache owners sharing their secrets to amazing geocaches, and opportunities to experience what makes geocaching in Australia so special.

After a casual evening meet-and-greet event the night prior, the day of the Block Party was a gorgeous cloudless day. Under the strong Australian sun, we all gathered for some opening remarks and a group picture. Following the opening ceremony, we were able to enjoy everything that the organizing committee, part of Geocaching Victoria, planned.

Gadget caches made by creative community members for the Adventure Lab® Caches were popular. I enjoyed solving them with other geocachers and appreciating the work it took to build them. The organizers also put together a great roster of informational sessions. Various geocachers gave presentations on crafting and hiding amazing geocaches. This included many types of caches ranging from EarthCaches to Letterboxes and challenge caches. Geocaching Victoria’s GPS Maze also made an appearance. It was a delight to walk through the educational labyrinth and especially to learn about geocaching in Australia.

I had the opportunity to participate in a question and answer session with local geocaching community volunteer reviewers Bunjil and Balayang. I enjoyed hearing the questions from the community and answering some myself.

The weekend wrapped up with a Cache In Trash Out® (CITO) at the Holden Flora Reserve on Sunday which was an amazing chance to help support the rich local environment with various improvement projects. Finally, after our work was complete, it was time for the final Event of the weekend and to say goodbye after three fun-filled days.

Even on the third day of attending all the Block Party fun, I was constantly meeting new geocachers. The design of the event created many opportunities to connect with everyone. The community was so friendly and welcoming! I had many wonderful conversations with cachers from around Australia. I especially loved learning about all the amazing geocaches and sights throughout the country.

I manage the Mega-Event program at HQ, so it was also incredibly rewarding to meet the members of Geocaching Victoria. I’ve supported their events through my role for several years now, and they were just as kind and passionate about geocaching in person!

An enormous thank you to the Block Party committee, especially RoamingHowie and Connie from ConnieandRick, who planned a spectacular celebration of the friendly community, the uniqueness of Australia, the fun of hiding new geocaches, and of course—25 years of geocaching!

Geocaching HQ Lackeys attend dozens of Mega and Giga-Events around the world, shaking hands, sharing stories of adventure, and of course, geocaching! em_adventuring is Community Special Events Manager at Geocaching HQ. She recently traveled to Australia to attend the Sunbury Event Block Party (GCAP417)

item.title: Four ways to celebrate Earth Day 2025
item.description:
There has never been a better day to care for the geocaching gameboard than today. Earth Day started in 1970 to raise awareness about environmental issues and inspire action. As we prepare to celebrate its 55th anniversary on April 22, we want to share some ideas of how you can celebrate Earth Day this year!

Geocaching, a game that owes its existence to our incredible Earth, offers a unique way to connect with the planet. It encompasses every biome imaginable, from tundras to rainforests and everything in between. Each Earth Day, we remember and celebrate the place we call home. Geocachers, with their unique connection to the Earth through geocaching, play a pivotal role in this celebration.

Here are four ways to give back to our planet and celebrate Earth Day through geocaching:

Attend a CITO Event near you
Attending a Cache In Trash Out® (CITO) Event is a great way to give back to the Earth. Every time you collect a bag of trash, clean up a park, or plant a tree, you contribute to our goal of leaving the global geocaching gameboard better than we found it.

Since 2002, more than 773,000 geocachers have attended over 43,000 CITO Events across 152 countries, helping improve the geocaching gameboard. If you attend a CITO Event now through May 31, 2025, you’ll also earn the CITO Season 1 souvenir for your Geocaching profile. Find a CITO Event near you!

Find an EarthCache
An EarthCache is more than just a set of coordinates; it’s a special place that offers a unique learning experience about our Earth’s geoscience features. Geocachers who visit EarthCaches can witness how geological processes shape our planet.

EarthCaches provide a fun geocaching experience and a unique opportunity to learn about the Earth’s geological features, making them a valuable educational tool for all geocachers this Earth Day. Find an EarthCache near you!

Reuse!
This is the season for some cleaning, an ideal time to declutter and collect miscellaneous items that could be repurposed into new geocaches. Instead of throwing out your trash or recyclables, we suggest you make a cool cache container, some interesting swag, or assign a tracking code and send it off as a trackable. The possibilities are endless!

Get outside
As geocachers, we’re part of an adventurous community that values the power of getting outdoors and spending time in fresh air. This game allows us to appreciate the natural beauty outside our homes and is a respite from our busy lives. Earth Day is the perfect opportunity to get outside and enjoy all that nature has to offer around us. It’s a chance to connect with fellow geocachers and share our love for the game and the planet.

How are you planning to celebrate Earth Day 2025? We’d love to hear about your geocaching adventures and how you’re giving back to our planet. Share your plans and inspire others to join in the celebration!

item.title: SNOOPY IN MIROW—Geocache of the Week
item.description:
Traditional Cache
GC9B4PC
by eddysnz
Difficulty:
2.5
Terrain:
1.5
Location:
Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Germany
N 53° 17.305 E 012° 47.826

“Keep looking up… That’s the secret of life.” – Snoopy, Peanuts

This geocache has more than just words of wisdom to share; it has secrets, too. Take a snooze with us as we visit this beloved character at our Geocache of the Week, SNOOPY IN MIROW (GC9B4PC).

Nearly everyone can recognize Snoopy, the beloved beagle and backyard philosopher from Charles M Schultz’s Peanuts comics. Alongside his best friend and sidekick, Woodstock, he often gets lost in daydreams, usually atop his iconic red doghouse.

Now, geocachers can join in on those adventures as they visit SNOOPY IN MIROW (GC9B4PC)!

The adventure begins on the lakeshore of Mirrower See, where several interesting sculptures and installations can be found. From a giant ant next to a canoe, to a precariously leaning lighthouse and a pair of wooden carved people lounging on a bench, there’s certainly a lot to see at this lake.

For geocachers, however, there’s one sculpture in particular to look out for.

On the edge of the clearing, bordering the reedy lakeshore, Snoopy waits, lost in a daydream as he faces the sky.

Is he deep in philosophical thought? Fantasizing about soaring through the sky as the Flying Ace? Or perhaps just snoozing?

That’s up to the geocacher to decide. For now, there’s just one thing that we’re daydreaming about: finding that geocache.

Instructions on the cache page will lead searchers to a combination code. For this next part, geocachers will go where Snoopy himself rarely does: his doghouse.

The geocache container sits safely under Snoopy’s watchful eye, just waiting to be found. Complete with a miniature hammock and table, even trackables can have a little rest here.

This find may be quick, but it’s a legacy long in the making. Since his start in 1950, Snoopy has delighted millions as he became one of the most iconic canine characters in the world.

This cache reminds us to “keep looking up” because there’s often something grand right around the corner. In this case, what we were searching for was with us all along.

item.title: We asked you: what advice do you have for new geocache hiders?
item.description:
Thinking about hiding your first geocache? You’re not alone! Placing a cache is a great way to give back to the game and connect with the community—but it also comes with some responsibility. To help you get started, we asked geocachers to share their tips for first-time cache hiders.

From choosing the right location to writing a great cache page, here’s what they had to say!
Note: some of the responses have been edited for clarity and brevity.

“I tell newbies to log onto the main website, check out tutorial videos and use the Help Center.” – Kevin A.

“Doublecheck your coordinates and stand by to respond to problems and maintenance needs for as long as your cache is active” – Cornflakes

“Just because it was a ‘container’ in a previous life – does NOT make it a good geocaching container.” – Roseanne T.

“Attend Events often. Events are the heart of geocaching, and it is at events where the geocaching community is built.” – Michael R.

“Make sure the cache container is in place before sending it in to be reviewed” – Jane R.

“Get permissions. Reach out to local land management to get permissions. Besides, the conversation could end up making your hide that much better. When the manager is excited about the cache, it makes it more fun for everyone.” – zumby65

“1) Read the guidelines
2) Read the guidelines
3) Read the guidelines
4) Try and hide the largest cache you can in a location” – Wayne D.

“Attend Events and ask questions from veteran cachers. Most of us love to help!” – Carol A.

“Find lots of different types of caches–50 or so before you do your first hide. Make sure your coordinates are accurate.” – Marge H.

“Think of your hides as a tour guide to visitors. What would entice the finder to look back on your hide with fond memories. Look back on your past 200+ finds & hide what will give that feeling to others.” – John C.

“Attend Events and ask others how they hid their caches and seek advice. This will save frustration with the geocaching community volunteer reviewers, who are amazing people that volunteer their precious time for Geocaching.” – Aditi M.

“Take your time picking the right location! A well-hidden geocache in a scenic or interesting spot makes the find more rewarding. Use durable, waterproof containers, and always test your coordinates multiple times before publishing. Most importantly, maintain your cache—regular upkeep keeps the game fun for everyone!” – Tonertime7

Ready to get started? Visit geocaching.com/play/hide to learn more and begin the cache submission process.

item.title: Celebrate Earth Day every day with the Planet WOW! GeoTour
item.description:
The Planet WOW! GeoTour (GT4FC) includes geocaches placed at destinations that WOW! across the United States.

The Planet WOW! GeoTour is a collaboration between Tinkercast, the creators of the #1 kids & family podcast “Wow in the World,” Aspen Institute’s Planet Media, The Nature Conservancy, and Geocaching HQ. Although the podcast is designed for kids ages 6–12 and their families, Planet WOW! welcomes all adventurers—young and young at heart—to embark on a trailblazing, audio-filled, action-packed adventure to places that WOW! After all, you have to love nature to want to protect it, right?

Planet WOW! geocaches include trackable Planet WOW! trading cards with WOW facts about caring for our climate. If you find a trading card in the wild, be sure to mention where you spotted it in your log—and include something that WOWed you about the location!

To learn more about the project, visit the Planet WOW! website where you can listen to exclusive podcasts from “Wow in the World” hosts Guy Raz and Mindy Thomas and print trading cards to place in geocaches near you.

To learn more about the Planet WOW! GeoTour (GT4FC), visit the landing page.

item.title: ROMANÓWKA — Geocache of the Week
item.description:
Traditional
GC5PPB8
by GMKłodzko
Difficulty:
1.5
Terrain:
1.5
Location:
Dolnośląskie, Poland
N 50° 20.847′ E 016° 42.903′

We’re seeing green with this geocache! Nothing screams “geocache” more than this gigantic geocaching ammo can container! Get ready for an extra large Geocache of the Week, ROMANÓWKA (GC5PPB8).

Finding an ammo can usually means that the cache is a Regular or Large size, but today, it means that it is larger than life! Cache owner GMKłodzko took “Large” to a whole new level with an ammo can big enough to stand in!

Due to its size, finding the geocache is a breeze, but unlocking it is a different story. The cache page contains some helpful hints to guide geocachers in cracking the code to open the container and access the logbook.

1. To open, look low at the back
2. To enter, look at the back

A tool of the trade is available to help geocachers easily access the cache.

Once the code is cracked, it’s time to climb inside, literally! It’s not every day that you can stand inside a cache container, so the owner added some fun extra elements, like a TB hotel to swap trackables and a place to trade SWAG.

Geocachers travel near and far to check this geocache off their bucket list:

To travel 400 km for one gearbox – priceless 😁😆🤣 – bojsiu17

This is a cache to remember, one that will fill you with big memories for years to come. While this geocache took some serious construction, the idea was a classic one. Geocachers love finding unique containers, and this one accomplished just that. Since 2015, this incredible cache has accumulated over 740 finds.

Want to make an impact on your community like GC5PPB8? Check out how you can hide your first geocache!

item.title: Geocaching International Film Festival 2025
item.description:
The GIFF saga continues!

As if there weren’t enough reasons to get excited for 2025, the Geocaching International Film Festival (GIFF) is back!

Geocaching is full of moments that should be captured and shared with the global geocaching community. Whether you prefer comedies, dramas, or sci-fi adventures, GIFF is an opportunity to enjoy stories (both fictional and real) about geocaching.

This year is all about celebration. Not only are we celebrating 25 years of geocaching, but the amazing community that has built this game for a quarter century. That’s why this year’s GIFF theme is “TFTC—Thanks For The Community!”

Do you have a geocaching story to tell? Submit your video May 6–July 31, 2025 on the GIFF website.

Then, share in the laughs, tears, and nail-biting action this November 6-16 with your fellow geocachers in-person or streaming online worldwide. Attend a GIFF Event to earn the GIFF 2025 souvenir.

Don’t change that channel! We’ll be right back with more information about submitting your own film and how to host or attend a GIFF Event near you.

Want to watch re-runs of GIFF? Check out previous years on the GIFF website.

item.title: 3 great ways to celebrate Geocaching in Your Pajamas Day
item.description:
Geocaching in Your Pajamas Day 2025 is coming up fast!

Inspired by National Wear Your Pajamas to Work Day, this first-time souvenir gives geocachers the chance to embrace the lighter side of life. Whether you spell it pajamas or pyjamas, it’s time to get your ‘snooze’ on and celebrate this silly sleepwear day in style!

To earn the souvenir, log any geocache, Adventure Lab® Location, or Event on April 16, 2025. How you decide to celebrate is up to you—the possibilities are endless!

Here are a few ideas to help you make Geocaching in Your Pajamas Day one to remember:

  1. Attend an Event! Pajama-themed Events are popping up around the globe in preparation for this ‘sleeptacular’ day. Attend wearing your best PJs, bring your morning cup of coffee, or use it as an excuse to wear sweatpants out of the house. Don’t forget to share pictures of the fun in your log!
  2. Do some early-morning caching. Are you a firm believer that pajamas are for the house only? No problem! Nab your souvenir by finding a cache before the birds wake up! Extra points if you can snap a picture of the sunrise.
  3. Solve a cozy Mystery Cache. Start your morning the right way—by solving a Mystery Cache in the comfort of your jammies! Find and log the cache that day to receive the souvenir!

Why count sheep when you can be counting your finds? Follow your dreams by earning this brand-new souvenir!

How will you celebrate Geocaching in Your Pajamas Day? Tell us in the comments below!

item.title: Bydir’s 10.000ste—Geocache of the Week
item.description:
Traditional Cache
GC6XWCC
by Bydir
Difficulty:
2.5
Terrain:
1.5
Location:
Flevoland, Netherlands
N 52° 27.115 E 005° 41.859

Who doesn’t love a nice, relaxing geocache? A whimsical birdhouse container that promises a quick and easy find.

Well, with this geocache, what you see isn’t necessarily what you get. Delight in the silly surprise with us as we flock to our Geocache of the Week, Bydir’s 10.000ste (GC6XWCC).

According to the cache page, GC6XWCC was placed for a special occasion. To celebrate local cacher Bydir’s 10,000 cache finds, Stipjes team helped to hide a new geocache… with a twist.

This cache may appear unassuming, but if we’ve learned one thing, it’s that a hide doesn’t need to be a Mystery Cache to be devious.

The geocache decor is thematically on-brand, even complete with a bird similar to Bydir’s profile picture. Perched on a piece of wood on one side of the birdhouse, geocachers might mistake this for a quaint, easy find.

They’ll soon realize, though, that this cache is anything but.

This feathery friend seems to have been ‘caching’ supplies in this birdhouse for quite some time. One might expect the sticks and branches birds use for their nests, but there’s another type of cache nestled away somewhere unexpected, ready for you to discover:

 

View this post on Instagram

 

A post shared by Geocaching (@geocaching)

Video by gc_anjoki.

Unlatching the bottom of the birdhouse, geocachers might take fright as dozens of identical tubes suddenly fall to the ground below.

This cache is an ‘egg’sellent example of why geocaching isn’t always for the faint of heart.

The most diabolical part of this hide? After this sudden surprise, you’ll realize it’s not over yet! But don’t let that ruffle your feathers.

Geocachers need to check each tube to locate the logbook hidden inside. Only then can they log this cache as Found and fly on to their next geocache.

This Geocache of the Week goes to show that birds of a feather flock together, especially when it comes to creating ingenious cache hides.

Celebrating your accomplishments with your geocaching community only strengthens the nest, leading to some spectacular things.

item.title: Celebrate the history of geocaching with M.E.G.A.
item.description:
As we approach geocaching’s 25th anniversary, we decided to celebrate in a BIG way this year.

Our team of geocaching historians sat down to find the best way to commemorate the history, cultural importance, and most importantly, joy, that comes with 25 years of geocaching.

Geocaching HQ is excited to officially introduce M.E.G.A.: The Museum of Exciting Geocaching Artifacts!

Visitors of M.E.G.A. can see exhibits highlighting geocaching’s origins and rich global history. Even the construction of the building itself is based on a part of geocaching history! The thick metal casing of the ammo can represents the strength of the geocaching community (with the added bonus of keeping the exhibits safe from the weather).

Here are just a few of the permanent exhibits that you can expect to see in M.E.G.A.:

  • Explore Methods of geocaching through the ages! From the historic paper map, printed online directions, and even the rare GPS device. You’ll get a blast from the past as you walk through the halls of caching history!
  • The world’s largest trackable collection (the largest collection was actually owned by a trackable enthusiast in Texas, so we had to create 150 new trackables to claim this title!): ‘Visit’ this exhibit to see some of the most famous trackables out there, including the famed Moun10Bike geocoin and a collection of Jeep trackables!
  • The life and adventures of Signal the Frog®: From a tiny tadpole to the celebrated geocaching mascot that he is today, this exhibit explores Signal’s journey to become a global geocaching phenomenon.

The exact location of M.E.G.A. is only accessible to players who solve the world’s most complicated Mystery Cache. The exact publication date of this cache will be delayed until construction of the museum is complete, but it is currently set as the first-ever Difficulty 10 geocache.

In the meantime, check out the museum’s temporary digital exhibit, Fool’s Gold: Geocaching Pranks Through The Ages, for a sneak peek at the sillier side of geocaching:

  1. Signal’s Ranch

    Ever wonder where geocaches come from? They grow on trees, of course!
    Locally grown on Geocaching HQ’s farm, Signal’s Ranch, fresh, organic, and non-GeoMO cache crops are picked at the peak of freshness, ready to hide.

  2. GeoLand

    Visit the first (and only) geocaching-themed amusement park! GeoLand offers rides and attractions that are sure to be fun for the whole family; take an adrenaline-pumping ride on The DNF Coaster, try not to get dizzy on the Tracker’s Tea-pups ride, and then hop on Signal’s Satellite Tour for an adventure to the stars! This park is set to open on April 1, 2027.

  3. Tera Events, Geocaching’s BIGGEST cache type yet

    Have you ever attended a Giga Event and thought, “This could be bigger?” Well, now you and 50,000 of your geo-pals can log a “will attend” for the BIGGEST geocaching event ever, the TERA Event.

  4. GeoPets Academy
    Tired of logging Owner Attention Requested logs? The GeoPets Academy can help! Enroll your geo-dog, cat, or ferret in the GeoPets Academy to help them learn geocache etiquette, general cache maintenance, and simple puzzle-solving to level up your geocaching. Come, sit, and stay at GeoPets Academy’s April 1, 2025, open house.

  5. Galaxy Caching: The Final Frontier

    On April 1, 2016, Geocaching HQ released a new feature for the website and mobile app to take your geocaching to new heights — literally. With Galaxy Search, players can now search for geocaches in space and plan your next galactic geocaching adventure.

  6. Journey to the Center of the EarthCache

    In 2015, the Geocaching HQ video team followed a team of brave geocachers on an endeavor that is unprecedented in the geocaching world. Their ultimate goal: to find the most difficult EarthCache in the world.

  7. Geocacher of the Month – Dean F.
    The Geocaching HQ Blog celebrates the things that make this game so amazing, like geocachers themselves! On April 1, 2014, HQ decided to honor a most notable and dedicated geocacher, Dean F., as Geocacher of the Month. With over 50,000 Did Not Find logs, Dean F. is truly an example of what a geocacher can (or can’t) do when they put their mind to it.

  8. T.I.N.Y.

    On April 1, 2013, a new geocache size entered the adventure of geocaching! T.I.N.Y. stands for Teentsy Infinitesimal Nucleic Yocto Geocache and measures approximately 1/10,000th of a Micro geocache. Small but mighty, this geocache size is for serious geocachers only.

  9. Cachers of Steel

    Inspired by the world’s favorite outdoor hobby, an all-new fitness fad swept the geocaching community by storm on April 1, 2012. Geocachers around the world learned new tricks of the trade with Geocaching HQ’s workout routine: Cachers of Steel.

item.title: Geocache of the Week Flashback Edition: Stonehenge in the Desert
item.description:
Traditional
GC6H1TZ
by Kris32
Difficulty:
1.5
Terrain:
1.5
Location:
Nevada, United States
N 35° 50.406 W 115° 16.068

Take a look at the picture above; do you notice something out of the ordinary? It’s not a mirage, and although it may seem too unbelievable to be real, there is a top-rated geocache nestled somewhere in the vicinity.

Come with us as we sweat our way to this Geocache of the Week, Stonehenge in the Dessert (GC6H1TZ).

Deserts are known to be unforgiving. With extreme weather conditions and water scarcity, you wouldn’t expect to see such a vibrant art installation here. “Seven Magic Mountains” is the name of this colorful, stacked boulder installation, located about 10 miles (16 km) south of Las Vegas, Nevada.

The installation highlights the intersection between the natural and artificial, shown in the exaggerated colors and stacking of these naturally formed rocks.

Similarly, geocaching connects humans to the natural world around them. Every day, geocachers get outdoors and forge new connections with their surroundings.

This unique site is no exception; if there’s one thing cachers love, it’s finding hidden treasures in the most unexpected places.

One cacher, Kris32, found the most unassuming location for GC6H1TZ. But hiding it from non-geocachers was vital to driving longevity, as many tourists visit Seven Magic Mountains year-round. Placing the cache a little trek away from the installation proved to add to the fun for many finders.

With so many unpredictable conditions, wildlife, and tourists that pass through, this cache had to be exchanged for a new container more than once. But no matter how many times this cache morphed into different containers, the one consistent thing has been the stealthy location.

Nestled underneath baby palm trees, you can find this camouflaged container chilling in the shade. After all, even caches need to cool off in such heat!

If you’re lucky, you might find a loaded stache with trackables and swag. Cachers have found everything from fuse bead hitchhikers to super cute swag in the form of minions. Whether you come for the thrill of the challenge, are looking to exchange fun swag, or want to help a trackable to its next destination, GC6H1TZ provides fun for anyone and everyone.

Many cachers have enjoyed their visit to this landmark and cache find, writing in their log entries:

Maybe my first cache trekking into the ‘wild’ lol. Very rocky but surprisingly, not too bad for noon in July. TFTC!” — ooozabe

“I love desert caches, thanks for the fun little walk out from the rocks. The cache is in great shape.” — MangoTheGecko

“My first Nevada find. Cool outdoor artwork. I would never have known of this if not for the highly liked geocache. Thank you for bringing me here and TFTC!” — HikeWalker

Don’t worry – if you get lost in the fun, the vibrant array of boulders will always be a north star, guiding you back.

For all the adventurers, take note that the listed attributes say the find should take less than an hour, but there are no amenities, and you could come across some slithery friends and creepy crawlers on their own geo-journey.

If you can get past some of the listed conditions on the cache page, this tourist-friendly landmark makes for a fun road trip pitstop.

The cache owner wrote “temporary art in the desert” in the description, as the installation was due to be removed by 2018, but its popularity granted an extension to 2027. So you have a bit more time to plan this cache into your next road trip.

Would you add this cache to your “must-visit” list?

Continue to explore some of the most amazing geocaches around the world.
Check out all of the Geocaches of the Week on the Geocaching blog. If you would like to nominate a Geocache of the Week, fill out this form.

item.title: New Souvenirs: Blue Switch Day 2025!
item.description:
It’s incredible to think that one small action could chart a course toward something so big. On May 2, 2000, that’s exactly what happened as the pivotal decision was made to flip the “Blue Switch,” leading to geocaching as we know it today.

On May 2, 2000, the United States government decided to discontinue restricting GPS accuracy, known as Selective Availability, making GPS technology more accurate for everyone. May 2 became known to geocachers as “Blue Switch Day.” The first geocache was hidden the following day on May 3, 2000.

This first hide started a chain of events that no one could have predicted. This eventually resulted in the game of geocaching, a global hobby with over 3.3 million geocaches!

This year, we depicted this important series of events with a Rube Goldberg Machine®. The many complex steps in the machine represent the complicated web of decisions that led from the removal of Selective Availability to modern geocaching, a hobby 25 years in the making.

To celebrate 25 years of geocaching, there are two new souvenirs to earn for Blue Switch Day 2025!

Blue Switch Day 2025 finder:

  • To earn this souvenir, geocachers must find and log one geocache, attend an Event, or complete an Adventure Lab® Location between May 2 and 4, 2025.

Blue Switch Day 2025 hider:

  • To earn this souvenir, publish a geocache between May 1 and 31, 2025
  • Events and Adventure Labs not included
  • Submit your geocache for review by May 24, 2025

Learn more about the cache review process in our Help Center.

How will you celebrate Blue Switch Day this year?

item.title: A recap of our first 2025 hiding theme: frogs! 🐸
item.description:
In 2025, we’re celebrating a major milestone—25 years of geocaching! To mark this special anniversary, we’re introducing a new hiding theme per quarter to celebrate geocaches published in 2025. Every three months, we’ll feature geocaches from that quarter’s theme on the Geocaching Blog and social media.

We received so many nominations for our first hiding theme, frogs, that it was difficult to choose just a few to share!

Take a look at some of the caches that “leapt” out to us:

GCAZHCK—⚡Signal⚡, o Batráquio!
Cache owner: Geocaching_CWB 🇧🇷

So simple, yet so creative! Pull out this frog’s “tongue” to expand the logbook!

GCB313Z—La grenouille grimpeuse 🐸
Cache owner: OusKonNé & Cétyla 🇨🇦

Better grab this cache quick, or he’ll climb away!

GCAV56W—Thaddeus zu Frankenhain
Cache owner: LetzterVersuch 🇩🇪

We’ve all heard the story of the frog prince. But searching for him, canister by canister? That’s a whole new challenge!

GCB3PR3—The Toad Stool
Cache owner: Shannifer 🇺🇸

This cache takes “toad stool” literally. This outhouse is even complete with a “log-roll” of toilet paper!

GCB2ZVN—🐸 Japanese Signal the Frog 🐸
Cache owner: _nokos_ 🇯🇵

 

View this post on Instagram

 

A post shared by TFTC!! GEOCACHING RADIO (@geocaching_radio)

That’s not a cone at all… that’s “Japanese Signal!” Have fun finding the logbook in this adorable and cleverly-disguised version of Signal the Frog®.

GCB3W46—SIGNALS WATERFRONT PAD
Cache owner: guitardreaming 🇨🇦

Where can you expect to find a frog? Why, on a lilypad, of course! This cache will require you to get your hands wet as you reel in your find.

GCB2X62—🐸 EL POZO DE LOS DESEOS #3
Cache owner: Myotragus 🇪🇸

How far would you go for a frog find? In this Terrain 5 adventure, you’ll need to climb down a well to reach the frog prince at the end!

GCB3RTD—Child’s Play: Finn the Frog
Cache owner: aurora_batty 🇺🇸

This cute little frog is sitting on a secret—literally! Locate the hidden key to unlock the logbook below.

GCAWQBE—Pienet sammakot 🐸 Little Frogs
Cache owner: copohontas 🇫🇮

The frogs guide the way in this intricate gadget cache! Count the frogs on each level to unlock the next section until you get to the logbook. Leap through levels of fun!

GCB3CTP—Békamentés
Cache owner: Dr.Lada 🇭🇺

This shows that Cache In Trash Out® Events can be beyond litter cleanup! This semiannual Event works with an organization to build ‘frog fences,’ structures that keep frogs away from busy highways near their habitat.

GCB3G85—Froggy Frolics
Cache owner: Nuttytart 🇬🇧

This clever cache already blends into its surroundings but also has a few tricks up its…branch?

GC6P7VV—Frog Prince
Cache owner: Holly Gillar 🇺🇸

This frog prince may be made of stone, but he’s still got a heart (and crown) of gold!

GCB3JEF—La Grenouille est sortie de l’étang
Cache owner: baro59 🇨🇭

This little frog left the pond, but he still found a way to make this log feel like home!

GCB3805—Frogs, Frogs, and More Frogs
Cache owner: emmieo 🇨🇦

Build the Signal puzzle to uncover the final coordinates and leap your way to the logbook!

GCB1MBM—Fly Boy
Cache owner: Perez8 🇺🇸

Fly Boy is a testament to building community after disaster. After a series of hurricanes, cache owners Perez8 CITO’d their way to something fun by creating this masterpiece from garage coach lights, roof soffit, fence post caps, tire lug nuts, trailer bearings, and rebar.Now that’s pretty fly!

These ambitious amphibians were a great way to kick off our 2025 Hiding Themes! Thank you to the cache owners who created fantastic frog-themed containers and everyone who nominated a geocache for the hiding theme! Visit #GeoHT25 on Instagram and the Hiding themes highlight on the @geocaching Instagram page to see more nominations from this quarter’s theme.

Our next theme is: Back to nature 🌲🍃

Visit the Back to nature blog for more details and inspiration on hiding your own nature-themed hide!
